jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety & Secruity Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

Environmental Health Safety & Security (EHS&S) Manager

Location:
Milgard Manufacturing, Sacramento, CA

Compensation Range:
$96,000.00 - $119,000.00 annually (depending on experience)

Work Hours:
Primarily day shift; schedule based on business needs

Job Summary

The EHS&S Manager is responsible for promoting and driving continuous improvement of environmental, health, safety, and security systems that reduce workplace incidents and ensure regulatory compliance. This role provides leadership, technical expertise, and strategic direction to management and employees on environmental, health, ergonomic, safety, and security initiatives. The EHS&S Manager partners with facility leadership to identify and address risks, implement preventative measures, ensure compliance with applicable regulations, and drive a culture of safety throughout the organization.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Lead and manage the facility’s environmental, health, safety, and security (EHS&S) programs and continuous improvement initiatives.
Develop, implement, and maintain EHS&S policies, procedures, and written programs including Lockout/Tagout, Confined Space Entry, Mobile Equipment Safety, Fall Protection, Electrical Safety, Hearing Conservation, Hazard Communication, Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), Emergency Action Plans, Security Programs, Bloodborne Pathogens, Waste Management, Spill Response, and Storm Water Management.
Ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, DOT, state, local, and company safety and environmental requirements.
Serve as the primary facility resource and contact for regulatory agencies and compliance-related matters.
Prepare, maintain, and submit all required environmental reports and documentation accurately and on time.
Manage the development and administration of Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs) and associated document control processes.
Lead the facility safety committee and partner with plant leadership to achieve company and site-specific safety objectives.
Conduct safety inspections, audits, and risk assessments to identify opportunities for improvement.
Develop and facilitate EHS&S training programs for employees and leadership teams.
Measure, analyze, and communicate key safety and environmental performance metrics.
Build and maintain accountability systems that reinforce safety ownership at all levels of the organization.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate EHS&S priorities into daily operations and business objectives.
Support Human Resources with new hire safety orientation and return-to-work programs.
Evaluate workplace hazards and implement effective controls to mitigate risk.
Conduct incident investigations and root cause analyses to identify corrective and preventive actions.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Strong knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental, health, and safety regulations and industry standards.
Working knowledge of manufacturing operations, processes, and safety practices.
Experience with construction and job site safety requirements.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to conduct training and present information to various audiences.
Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to identify root causes and implement effective corrective actions.
Proven organizational and project management skills.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to influence positive change across all levels of the organization.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, spreadsheets, databases, and presentation software.
Ability to read, write, speak, and comprehend English.
Emergency response, First Aid, and CPR training experience preferred.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Health & Safety, Occupational Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Environmental Science, Engineering, or a related field; or
Seven (7) years of related EHS experience and/or training; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience supporting safety programs within a manufacturing environment strongly preferred.
Demonstrated ability to maintain current knowledge of applicable federal, state, local, and company safety and environmental regulations.

Job Specific Requirements

Required to wear personal protective equipment (PPE) and comply with all company safety policies and procedures.
Ability to work in both office and manufacturing environments.
Ability to move throughout production, warehouse, and job site environments.
Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, bend, stoop, twist, and climb as needed.
Strong hand dexterity and physical mobility.
Minimal travel required.
Job-related information and requirements are subject to change based on business needs.

About MITER Brands

MITER Brands is one of the nation’s leading manufacturers of residential windows and doors, serving both the new construction and replacement markets. Founded in 1947, the company brings together a family of industry-leading brands united by a passion for quality, innovation, and a relentless pursuit of excellence. Its portfolio includes MI Windows and Doors, Milgard Windows & Doors, PGT Windows, Western Architectural Openings, Anlin Windows & Doors, and Sunrise Windows & Doors. With manufacturing facilities nationwide, MITER Brands is committed to a people-first culture that delivers exceptional products, outstanding customer experiences, and inspiring opportunities for team members, customers, and communities alike.

Ready to Grow Your Career?

Join a team that values safety, quality, collaboration, and continuous improvement. If you're looking for an opportunity to make an impact and build a rewarding career with a leading manufacturer, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to become part of the MITER Brands team.

What We Offer

At MITER Brands, we invest in your health, wealth, and wellness. Our comprehensive benefits package supports you and your eligible spouse/dependents while helping you achieve your personal and professional goals.

We offer competitive pay, a 401(k) with company match, and generous paid time off to help you maintain a healthy work-life balance.

Health & Wellness

Three comprehensive medical plan options
Prescription drug coverage
Dental insurance
Vision insurance
Teladoc virtual healthcare services
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Annual Wellness Clinic

Financial Protection

Company-paid Life Insurance
Voluntary Life Insurance

Company-paid Long-Term Disability

Additional Benefits

Paid Time Off (PTO) and paid holidays
401(k) retirement plan with company match
Tuition Reimbursement Program
Legal Insurance
Identity Theft Protection
Pet Insurance
Team Member Discount Program

MITER Brands, including MI Windows and Doors, Milgard, and PGT Innovations, is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, or any other protected status under applicable law.

jobs.title: Environmental Specialist II
jobs.description:
Company Description

Veolia in North America is the top-ranked environmental company in the United States for three consecutive years, and the country's largest private water operator and technology provider as well as hazardous waste and pollution treatment leader. It offers a full spectrum of water, waste, and energy management services, including water and wastewater treatment, commercial and hazardous waste collection and disposal, energy consulting and resource recovery. Veolia helps commercial, industrial, healthcare, higher education and municipality customers throughout North America. Headquartered in Boston, Veolia has more than 10,000 employees working at more than 350 locations across North America.

Job Description

Position Purpose:

This position provides specialized transportation and disposal services to our clients. Responsibilities include manifesting, packaging, spill clean-up response and remedial activities, labeling, loading, off loading & coordinating transportation, and sampling/profiling material while adhering to state and federal environmental, health, and safety regulations.

Primary Duties /Responsibilities

Sample and profile waste streams according to prescribed policies and procedures.
Manifesting, packaging, spill clean-up response and remedial activities, labeling, loading, off loading & coordinating transportation.
Knowledge of disposal site capabilities and limitations prior to shipment to ensure efficient disbursement and storage.
Maintain a professional image to clients by answering inquiries and suggesting solutions to existing/potential problems.
Comply and enforce all compliance, health, safety, and procedures in accordance with VES-TS policies.
Ensure completion of all paperwork in compliance with U. S. Department of Transportation (DOT)/Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) regulations and VES-TS policies and procedures.
Operate and maintain all equipment in a professional manner to ensure optimum efficiency and effectiveness to completion of project(s) in a timely manner.
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education / Experience / Background:

High School diploma or General Educational Development (GED) required
Bachelor's degree in Chemistry or a related science discipline preferred
Prior work experience in the hazardous waste/related industry required

Knowledge / Skills / Abilities

Strong team player
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
Time management: the ability to organize and manage multiple deadlines
Strong customer service orientation
Computer proficiency
Ability to follow through on assignments.

Required Certification / Licenses / Training

40-hour HAZWOPER Certification
A valid Driver's License
Ability to obtain a Class A or B Commercial Drivers License (CDL) with Hazardous (H) endorsement
Environmental Specialist II Competency Test

Additional Information

Pay Range:
$24 to $28.50 per hour

Benefits:
Veolia's comprehensive benefits package includes paid time off policies, as well as health, dental, vision, life insurance, savings accounts, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteering and more. In addition, employees are also entitled to participate in an employer sponsored 401(k) plan, to save for retirement.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer! All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

jobs.title: Lecturer in Environmental Science
jobs.description:
About us:

At the University of Canberra, we’re a welcoming and connected academic community shaped by the people, cultures and environments of Australia’s capital. Our research focuses on real-world challenges, working alongside partners to create outcomes that matter, while our teaching builds confidence and capability for the future. Ranked number one in Canberra for graduate employment, skills development and student support, UC is a place where you can grow ideas, contribute knowledge, and make a difference.

About the Faculty

The Faculty of Science & Health
is a dynamic and research-intensive academic community dedicated to improving health, wellbeing and quality of life through excellence in teaching, research, innovation and engagement.
Bringing together expertise across nursing, midwifery, rehabilitation, sport and exercise science, behavioural and human sciences, public health, psychology, social work, disability, biomedical science, environmental science and applied health sciences, the Faculty fosters a highly collaborative and interdisciplinary environment where researchers, educators and industry partners work together to address some of society's most pressing health, environmental and social challenges.

About the role:

We are seeking an enthusiastic and collaborative academic to join our Environmental Science team as a Lecturer in Environmental Science. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to a growing and research-active discipline while helping to educate the next generation of environmental professionals.
As a Lecturer, you will play a key role in delivering outstanding teaching, building a successful research profile, supervising student research projects, and engaging with industry, government and community partners. Your work will contribute to the University's commitment to addressing contemporary environmental challenges and strengthening our research impact.
Please note:
For this role, we are open to consider suitable candidates at either Lecturer (Academic Level B) or Senior Lecturer level (Academic Level C).

Key responsibilities:

Teach and coordinate undergraduate and postgraduate units in Environmental Science and related disciplines.
Deliver engaging and inclusive learning experiences across face-to-face, blended and online settings.
Design, review and enhance curriculum, assessment and learning resources to support student success and graduate employability.
Develop and grow a research program aligned with the University's environmental research strengths.
Publish high-quality research outputs and seek competitive research funding.
Supervise undergraduate research projects, Honours students and HDR candidates.
Maintain high standards of research integrity, ethics, safety and professional practice.

About you:

To be successful in this role, you will bring:
A completed doctoral qualification in Applied Environmental Science or a closely related discipline.
Demonstrated ability to teach and convene relevant units effectively across face-to-face, blended and online modes.
Demonstrated capacity to supervise undergraduate projects, Honours students, and HDR candidates effectively.
Expertise in an area aligned with the current research strengths in Applied Environmental Science: freshwater ecology, ecosystem processes, conservation ecology, genomics, or related fields
A developing or established track record of high-quality research publications.
Excellent communication, organisational and interpersonal skills.
A commitment to inclusion, diversity, cultural safety and student-centred learning.

Offerings/ Benefits/ Culture:

The University offers excellent conditions and benefits which can be further explored on our “Work at UC” site such as flexible, family-friendly policies, on site gym, on site medical services, a grocery store, and Early Childhood Education and Care facilities.
We believe people deserve to feel welcome, supported, and empowered to realise their potential. Being a values based organisation, UC sets a goal to be the national sector leader in equity, diversity, inclusion and access via our Reconnected Strategy. UC encourages applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability, neurodiversity and people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.

Eligibility:

Applicants who wish to apply for this position should have valid working rights at the time of submission.
The University of Canberra is committed to the safety of vulnerable and young people. As such, successful applicants will be required to have a current ACT working with vulnerable people registration. For further details on how to apply please click https://www.accesscanberra.act.gov.au

How to apply:

Please apply with you CV and a one-page cover letter outlining your interest and suitability. Also, please ensure you take the time to align your CV with the Position Description requirements. We want to understand how your skills and experience relate to the position you are applying for
If you are initially shortlisted, you may be asked to complete an online one-way video interview. There will be a list of pre-set questions that will need to be answered within a stipulated time.

For job specific information:
please contact Claire O'Brien- Head of School, Science - claire.obrien@canberra.edu.au
For recruitment and application questions:
please contact the Talent Solutions team on 02 6206 3867 or email uctalent@canberra.edu.au. We recognise people communicate and process information differently, and we support multiple ways to participate in the recruitment evaluation. For reasonable adjustment, please reach out to the UCTalent team.

Closing date: 11.55pm, Wednesday 11 November 2026

jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
This role is located at 62 Lake Mirror Road Forest Park, GA 30297.

Job Summary

Environmental Specialist is responsible for developing, communicating, and implementing waste related environmental programs, evaluating environmental data, ensuring regulatory compliance for various company business units and facilities, in a safe, compliant, and cost-effective manner. This role involves ensuring proper characterization and disposal of various environmental media, working with various waste vendors, Environmental regulators (State and Federal), transporters, TSDFs, conducting site visits and providing on-site guidance for on-going projects, and providing recommendations to minimize environmental risks and promote responsible environmental stewardship.

Work Responsibilites

Combination of office work and field activities.
May involve travel to facilities, project sites, or regulatory meetings.
Occasional work in construction, utility, or environmental remediation settings.
Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) may be required during field inspections.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, biology, chemistry, or a related field.
Minimum 5 years of environmental compliance or environmental management experience.
Knowledge of environmental regulations such as:
Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA)
Toxic Substance Control Act (TSCA)
Emergency Planning and Community Right to Know Act (EPCRA)
Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA)
Superfund Amendments and Reauthorization Act (SARA)
Georgia Hazardous Waste Management Act
OSHA environmental requirements
Department of Transportation (DOT)
Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasures Act (SPCC)
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.

Preferred Qualifications

Professional certifications such as:
Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM)
Certified Environmental Professional (CEP)
Qualified Environmental Professional (QEP)
Experience working with regulatory agencies and compliance programs.

Key Responsibilities

Waste Management and Compliance

Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local environmental regulations.
Identify, classify, and manage hazardous and non-hazardous waste.
Coordinate waste disposal activities with approved vendors and treatment facilities.

Waste Characterization and Tracking

Evaluate waste streams to determine proper handling and disposal methods.
Maintain waste profiles, manifests, and tracking records.
Monitor waste generation trends and identify opportunities for reduction.
Ensure accurate labeling, storage, and transportation of waste materials.

Operational Support

Inspect waste accumulation areas for compliance and safety.
Coordinate with operations, maintenance, and other site personnel.
Ensure waste handling equipment is properly maintained and used safely.
Conduct environmental inspections and audits.

Training Awareness

Train employees in waste handling procedures and environmental requirements.
Communicate regulatory changes and best practices.
Develop standard operating procedures (SOPs) for waste management activities.

Key Skills

Environmental compliance management
Waste characterization and classification
Regulatory reporting
Hazardous material handling
Data analysis and recordkeeping
Vendor management
Auditing and inspections
Problem solving and continuous improvement

Required

This position has been identified as a role that will require the use of a Georgia Power fleet vehicle. The following will be required if you are selected for this position:

Must have at least one year of verifiable driving experience (Must hold a valid driver’s license for the class vehicle to be operated. Driving permits are not typically considered a valid driver’s license).
Must have no revocation of driving privileges within the 36 months prior to application, no convictions of major traffic violations (DUI, hit and run, reckless driving, etc.) within the 12 months prior to application, or any pending charges for a major traffic violation at the time of application.
Must consent to Motor Vehicle Driver’s Record Monitoring via GPC Fleet Management.
Must consent to random drug testing .

Georgia Power
is the largest electric subsidiary of Southern Company (NYSE: SO), America's premier energy company. Value, Reliability, Customer Service and Stewardship are the cornerstones of the Company's promise to 2.6 million customers in all but four of Georgia's 159 counties. Committed to delivering clean, safe, reliable, and affordable energy at rates below the national average, Georgia Power maintains a diverse, innovative generation mix that includes nuclear, coal and natural gas, as well as renewables such as solar, hydroelectric and wind. Georgia Power focuses on delivering world-class service to its customers every day and the Company is recognized by J.D. Power and Associates as an industry leader in customer satisfaction. For more information, visit www.GeogiaPower.com and connect with the Company on Facebook (Facebook.com/GeorgiaPower), Twitter (Twitter.com/GeorgiaPower) and Instagram (Instagram.com/ga_power).

Southern Company (NYSE: SO ) is a leading energy provider serving 9 million customers across the Southeast and beyond through its family of companies. Providing clean, safe, reliable and affordable energy with excellent service is our mission. The company has electric operating companies in three states, natural gas distribution companies in four states, a competitive generation company, a leading distributed energy solutions provider with national capabilities, a fiber optics network and telecommunications services. Through an industry-leading commitment to innovation, resilience and sustainability, we are taking action to meet customers' and communities' needs while advancing our goal of net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. Our uncompromising values ensure we put the needs of those we serve at the center of everything we do and are the key to our sustained success. We are transforming energy into economic, environmental and social progress for tomorrow. Our corporate culture has been recognized by a variety of organizations, earning the company awards and recognitions that reflect Our Values and dedication to service. To learn more, visit www.southerncompany.com .

Southern Company invests in the well-being of its employees and their families through a comprehensive total rewards strategy that includes competitive base salary, annual incentive awards for eligible employees and health, welfare and retirement benefits designed to support physical, financial, and emotional/social well-being. This position may also be eligible for additional compensation, such as an incentive program, with the amount of any bonus/awards subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan(s). A summary of the benefits offered for this position can be found here https://seo.nlx.org/southernco/pdf/SOCO-Benefits.pdf . Additional and specific details about total compensation and beneﬁts will also be provided during the hiring process.

new_jobs.title: Lecturer in Environmental Science
new_jobs.description:
About us:

At the University of Canberra, we’re a welcoming and connected academic community shaped by the people, cultures and environments of Australia’s capital. Our research focuses on real-world challenges, working alongside partners to create outcomes that matter, while our teaching builds confidence and capability for the future. Ranked number one in Canberra for graduate employment, skills development and student support, UC is a place where you can grow ideas, contribute knowledge, and make a difference.

About the Faculty

The Faculty of Science & Health
is a dynamic and research-intensive academic community dedicated to improving health, wellbeing and quality of life through excellence in teaching, research, innovation and engagement.
Bringing together expertise across nursing, midwifery, rehabilitation, sport and exercise science, behavioural and human sciences, public health, psychology, social work, disability, biomedical science, environmental science and applied health sciences, the Faculty fosters a highly collaborative and interdisciplinary environment where researchers, educators and industry partners work together to address some of society's most pressing health, environmental and social challenges.

About the role:

We are seeking an enthusiastic and collaborative academic to join our Environmental Science team as a Lecturer in Environmental Science. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to a growing and research-active discipline while helping to educate the next generation of environmental professionals.
As a Lecturer, you will play a key role in delivering outstanding teaching, building a successful research profile, supervising student research projects, and engaging with industry, government and community partners. Your work will contribute to the University's commitment to addressing contemporary environmental challenges and strengthening our research impact.
Please note:
For this role, we are open to consider suitable candidates at either Lecturer (Academic Level B) or Senior Lecturer level (Academic Level C).

Key responsibilities:

Teach and coordinate undergraduate and postgraduate units in Environmental Science and related disciplines.
Deliver engaging and inclusive learning experiences across face-to-face, blended and online settings.
Design, review and enhance curriculum, assessment and learning resources to support student success and graduate employability.
Develop and grow a research program aligned with the University's environmental research strengths.
Publish high-quality research outputs and seek competitive research funding.
Supervise undergraduate research projects, Honours students and HDR candidates.
Maintain high standards of research integrity, ethics, safety and professional practice.

About you:

To be successful in this role, you will bring:
A completed doctoral qualification in Applied Environmental Science or a closely related discipline.
Demonstrated ability to teach and convene relevant units effectively across face-to-face, blended and online modes.
Demonstrated capacity to supervise undergraduate projects, Honours students, and HDR candidates effectively.
Expertise in an area aligned with the current research strengths in Applied Environmental Science: freshwater ecology, ecosystem processes, conservation ecology, genomics, or related fields
A developing or established track record of high-quality research publications.
Excellent communication, organisational and interpersonal skills.
A commitment to inclusion, diversity, cultural safety and student-centred learning.

Offerings/ Benefits/ Culture:

The University offers excellent conditions and benefits which can be further explored on our “Work at UC” site such as flexible, family-friendly policies, on site gym, on site medical services, a grocery store, and Early Childhood Education and Care facilities.
We believe people deserve to feel welcome, supported, and empowered to realise their potential. Being a values based organisation, UC sets a goal to be the national sector leader in equity, diversity, inclusion and access via our Reconnected Strategy. UC encourages applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability, neurodiversity and people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.

Eligibility:

Applicants who wish to apply for this position should have valid working rights at the time of submission.
The University of Canberra is committed to the safety of vulnerable and young people. As such, successful applicants will be required to have a current ACT working with vulnerable people registration. For further details on how to apply please click https://www.accesscanberra.act.gov.au

How to apply:

Please apply with you CV and a one-page cover letter outlining your interest and suitability. Also, please ensure you take the time to align your CV with the Position Description requirements. We want to understand how your skills and experience relate to the position you are applying for
If you are initially shortlisted, you may be asked to complete an online one-way video interview. There will be a list of pre-set questions that will need to be answered within a stipulated time.

For job specific information:
please contact Claire O'Brien- Head of School, Science - claire.obrien@canberra.edu.au
For recruitment and application questions:
please contact the Talent Solutions team on 02 6206 3867 or email uctalent@canberra.edu.au. We recognise people communicate and process information differently, and we support multiple ways to participate in the recruitment evaluation. For reasonable adjustment, please reach out to the UCTalent team.

Closing date: 11.55pm, Wednesday 11 November 2026

new_jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
new_jobs.description:
This role is located at 62 Lake Mirror Road Forest Park, GA 30297.

Job Summary

Environmental Specialist is responsible for developing, communicating, and implementing waste related environmental programs, evaluating environmental data, ensuring regulatory compliance for various company business units and facilities, in a safe, compliant, and cost-effective manner. This role involves ensuring proper characterization and disposal of various environmental media, working with various waste vendors, Environmental regulators (State and Federal), transporters, TSDFs, conducting site visits and providing on-site guidance for on-going projects, and providing recommendations to minimize environmental risks and promote responsible environmental stewardship.

Work Responsibilites

Combination of office work and field activities.
May involve travel to facilities, project sites, or regulatory meetings.
Occasional work in construction, utility, or environmental remediation settings.
Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) may be required during field inspections.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, biology, chemistry, or a related field.
Minimum 5 years of environmental compliance or environmental management experience.
Knowledge of environmental regulations such as:
Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA)
Toxic Substance Control Act (TSCA)
Emergency Planning and Community Right to Know Act (EPCRA)
Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA)
Superfund Amendments and Reauthorization Act (SARA)
Georgia Hazardous Waste Management Act
OSHA environmental requirements
Department of Transportation (DOT)
Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasures Act (SPCC)
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.

Preferred Qualifications

Professional certifications such as:
Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM)
Certified Environmental Professional (CEP)
Qualified Environmental Professional (QEP)
Experience working with regulatory agencies and compliance programs.

Key Responsibilities

Waste Management and Compliance

Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local environmental regulations.
Identify, classify, and manage hazardous and non-hazardous waste.
Coordinate waste disposal activities with approved vendors and treatment facilities.

Waste Characterization and Tracking

Evaluate waste streams to determine proper handling and disposal methods.
Maintain waste profiles, manifests, and tracking records.
Monitor waste generation trends and identify opportunities for reduction.
Ensure accurate labeling, storage, and transportation of waste materials.

Operational Support

Inspect waste accumulation areas for compliance and safety.
Coordinate with operations, maintenance, and other site personnel.
Ensure waste handling equipment is properly maintained and used safely.
Conduct environmental inspections and audits.

Training Awareness

Train employees in waste handling procedures and environmental requirements.
Communicate regulatory changes and best practices.
Develop standard operating procedures (SOPs) for waste management activities.

Key Skills

Environmental compliance management
Waste characterization and classification
Regulatory reporting
Hazardous material handling
Data analysis and recordkeeping
Vendor management
Auditing and inspections
Problem solving and continuous improvement

Required

This position has been identified as a role that will require the use of a Georgia Power fleet vehicle. The following will be required if you are selected for this position:

Must have at least one year of verifiable driving experience (Must hold a valid driver’s license for the class vehicle to be operated. Driving permits are not typically considered a valid driver’s license).
Must have no revocation of driving privileges within the 36 months prior to application, no convictions of major traffic violations (DUI, hit and run, reckless driving, etc.) within the 12 months prior to application, or any pending charges for a major traffic violation at the time of application.
Must consent to Motor Vehicle Driver’s Record Monitoring via GPC Fleet Management.
Must consent to random drug testing .

Georgia Power
is the largest electric subsidiary of Southern Company (NYSE: SO), America's premier energy company. Value, Reliability, Customer Service and Stewardship are the cornerstones of the Company's promise to 2.6 million customers in all but four of Georgia's 159 counties. Committed to delivering clean, safe, reliable, and affordable energy at rates below the national average, Georgia Power maintains a diverse, innovative generation mix that includes nuclear, coal and natural gas, as well as renewables such as solar, hydroelectric and wind. Georgia Power focuses on delivering world-class service to its customers every day and the Company is recognized by J.D. Power and Associates as an industry leader in customer satisfaction. For more information, visit www.GeogiaPower.com and connect with the Company on Facebook (Facebook.com/GeorgiaPower), Twitter (Twitter.com/GeorgiaPower) and Instagram (Instagram.com/ga_power).

Southern Company (NYSE: SO ) is a leading energy provider serving 9 million customers across the Southeast and beyond through its family of companies. Providing clean, safe, reliable and affordable energy with excellent service is our mission. The company has electric operating companies in three states, natural gas distribution companies in four states, a competitive generation company, a leading distributed energy solutions provider with national capabilities, a fiber optics network and telecommunications services. Through an industry-leading commitment to innovation, resilience and sustainability, we are taking action to meet customers' and communities' needs while advancing our goal of net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. Our uncompromising values ensure we put the needs of those we serve at the center of everything we do and are the key to our sustained success. We are transforming energy into economic, environmental and social progress for tomorrow. Our corporate culture has been recognized by a variety of organizations, earning the company awards and recognitions that reflect Our Values and dedication to service. To learn more, visit www.southerncompany.com .
